title: Stock Market Today Highlights, Nov 12: Markets extend gains for 3rd day; Sensex ends above 81,900 on FII inflows, lower crude oil - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Percentage sign on top of coin stacks before blue financial graph. Horizontal composition with copy space. Business and finance concept. | Photo Credit: MicroStockHub

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 31.61 points, or 0.04%, to settle at 81,911.01. The 50-share NSE Nifty was up 44.30 points, or 0.18%, to end at 25,299.35.

Among the Sensex firms, Bajaj Finance, State Bank of India, Bharat Electronics, Bajaj Finserv, ICICI Bank and Eternal were the major winners. Hindustan Unilever, Maruti, Power Grid and Tata Consultancy Services were among the laggards.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹12,563.33 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, dipped 0.44% to $92.50 per barrel.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.73 against the dollar. During intra-day trade, it witnessed a high of 93.62 and a low of 94.06. The local unit settled at 94.04 (provisional), lower by 33 paise from its previous close.

Fairfax's Rs 52,878-crore IDBI Bank deal aims to integrate Digit insurance and IIFL Capital businesses into a diversified financial services platform.

Oil India posted standalone PAT of Rs 22.59 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs 10.44 crore in Q2FY26

Board approved interim dividend of Rs 7 per share.

Aditya Birla Capital opens its 100th Gold Loan branch in Santacruz, Mumbai, marking a rapid expansion into the market.

Zydus Lifesciences completes subscription to a 50% stake in Zydus Sunshine Lifesciences, forming an equal joint venture with Sunshine Healthcare Lanka.

Refex Industries' ash and coal handling order book reaches Rs 1,721 crore, as revenue grows 54.7% and the company expands into concrete and wind energy.

AI will create 10.6 million jobs and eliminate 8.9 million by 2030, while 435.5 million workers worldwide face changes to their roles, Gartner projects.

India's stock market has overtaken Taiwan to reclaim fifth place globally, with market capitalisation at $5.4 trillion amid strong FPI inflows.

Dilip Buildcon has been declared as L-1 bidder for the tender floated by the Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL).

Top gainers: HDFC Life (+3.93%), Shriram Finance (+3.28%), Bajaj Finance (+3.23%), SBI Life (+2.64%), SBI (+2.35%)

Top losers: M&M (-2.25%), Nestle (-1.93%), Power Grid (-1.86%), TCS (-1.56%), HUL (-1.55%)

Jupiter Life Line Hospitals has received LOI permission from the Thane Municipal Corporation for the expansion of its existing Thane Hospital.

“While the rupee slipped to 93.77 against the US dollar in early trade today, weighed down by a stronger dollar and rising US Treasury yields, these near-term fluctuations should not overshadow the broader recovery in the currency over recent weeks, bringing it back to levels last seen in April 2026. India is increasingly being viewed as a potential ‘AI hedge’ by global investors, with any further unwinding of crowded US and global AI-related trades potentially supporting foreign equity inflows into Indian markets. Alongside easing crude oil prices, these developments could provide further support to the rupee, with scope for consolidation in the 92.00–93.00 range in the coming weeks. However, the extent of appreciation may be moderated by RBI intervention aimed at rebuilding foreign exchange reserves, while renewed crude oil volatility and broader global uncertainties remain key risks to this outlook.”

Dabur India is betting big on premiumisation. The homegrown FMCG aims to grow the share of premium products to 23 per cent over the next 18 months. The company’s premium portfolio now spans across categories from health and wellness to beverages. Besides new launches, the company’s premium strategy includes contemporising its portfolio with new formats and new packaging. Read more

ZF Steering Gear (India): DriveSys Systems Private Limited (DriveSys), a wholly owned subsidiary, commenced commercial production under its Aluminium Division at its factory premises situated in Maharashtra.

The Reserve Bank of India is working on proposals that would prevent private ‌equity firms from holding a controlling stake in more than one non-bank lender, two people with knowledge of the plans said.

It is concerned that financial ⁠stress at a global private equity firm or its affiliates could have a contagion effect across several non-bank lenders in which it has significant investments, they said. Read more

Page Industries’ net profit inched up 4% to Rs 202.54 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs 194.76 crore in Q2FY26.

Declared 2nd interim dividend of Rs 150 per share.

Shares traded 9% lower at Rs 33,570 on the NSE.

HEG Advanced Material made an exchange filing today morning stating that its wholly owned subsidiary – TACC – has signed a nonbinding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a global lithium-ion cell manufacturer, for a proposed long-term supply of upto 40,000 tonnes of synthetic graphite-based Anode Active Material (AAM) for electric mobility applications.

The parties will work towards a progressive supply arrangement subject to further discussions and finalisation of technical and commercial requirements of both parties.

Standard Chartered (“the Bank”) today announced the launch of its wealth solutions from India’s Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City), expanding the international investment solutions available to its affluent clients in India.
